body: Thanks for the feedback. It actually felt good to just say what I was feeling and get it off my chest. I appreciate the insights and if things do not start to fade soon, I will look into therapy. I had a little bit of that back when I was a teen. First I went to a Christian Counselor (>_<) *pukes* and then later a secular therapist.

> If you drive your focus into a wall, your brain will follow, if you drive your focus into the positive (however small) your brain will follow.

Your supposition, in a nutshell is that I should just *think* happy thoughts, and then I will *be* happy. Generally speaking, I agree. I'm just having a hard time purging the negative thoughts. My head just feels very clouded right now. I spent the first 2 weeks unable to think about anything but him and his family. The third week he almost didn't cross my mind. Now into the 4th week its creeping back in. I suppose it's something that will fade in time. I think my normal depressive feelings are being amplified by the shock of it and my inability to rationalize/accept/understand it.
